correctness.rationale: For any n>=5, stationary minority iff each vertex has at most two like-minded neighbors, majority iff at least two. The 16-state four-window transfer graph gives a bijection between labelled stationary configurations and closed walks. Explicit complement-symmetry reduction yields four exact determinant factors, checked independently from the local rule using integer symbolic algebra. Exact matrix trace identities give every n count; Perron-Frobenius on the primitive minority positive block and algebraic estimates on remaining quintic/cubic roots establish unique leading eigenvalues. Independent exhaustive simulation and integer traces coincide for all n=5..16 for each rule. No claims about other periodic points or transients.

originality.rationale: Extant general finite-state enumeration techniques (Banks-Djirar 1993), radius-one majority fixed counts (Agur-Fraenkel-Klein 1988), structural radius-r characterization (Nakar-Ron 2022) and physical metastability treatments (Waclaw-Burda 2008) do not in inspected material state the explicit simultaneous degree-five/degree-three spectral fixed-state laws on C_n squared nor their quantified entropy ratio. A complete 1994 Moran radius-r majority text was unavailable, leaving a specific historical-priority risk; algorithmic computability is not confused with a recorded closed-form census. Searches of published mathematical records identified nearby claims involving different rules, states, or topologies. This is a qualified originality assessment, not proof that no equivalent published formula exists.
residual_risks: The full Moran (1994) article was inaccessible; priority of the majority-side census may be partly or fully covered there.

value.rationale: The square of a cycle is a natural fixed-valence, highly frustrated test family. Obtaining explicit low-degree transfer spectra for both repulsive and attractive tie-preserving updates and proving a strict entropy density gap on exactly the same graph is a motivated infinite-family dynamical invariant, quantitatively distinguishing stationary structure under opposing local rules. The result is not merely a small n table or a claim of new generic methodology.
